claim.quote: The results show that SSG are sensitive to recoil energies down to $\sim$1keV.

name: Detection of nuclear recoils in prototype dark matter detectors, made from Al, Sn and Zn Superheated Superconducting Granules

summary.plain: Bern physicists hit small tin, aluminium and zinc granule detectors with a neutron beam and showed that they respond to nuclear recoils down to about 1 keV, the kind of energy a dark matter particle would deposit.
summary.technical: Prototype SSG detectors (0.1 cm^3, Sn, Al and Zn) irradiated with a 70 MeV neutron beam, nuclear recoil energies from neutron scattering angles with a hodoscope; the abstract describes it as part of a project to develop an SSG detector for cold dark matter and neutrinos.

title: Detection of nuclear recoils in prototype dark matter detectors, made from Al, Sn and Zn Superheated Superconducting Granules
why_it_matters: The abstract says the limited angular resolution of the hodoscope prevented measuring the sensitivity at even lower recoil energies.
